# Search view — M3 guidance

<!-- Generated by apps/site/scripts/one-off/migrate-guidance.mjs. Do not edit by hand.
     The component pages carry the reference; this file carries the guidance. -->

## Web

### Features

Reach for the search view when finding needs a palette: the command-palette dialog over suggestions with an optional global hotkey. `suggestions` are data — id, title, optional description, keywords and leading node — filtered live as the query changes, with the query trio making it controlled or uncontrolled and `onSearch` the explicit submit, separate from typing. The hotkey opens the palette from anywhere on the page and opting out is one prop, while `label` and `placeholder` name the field. There is no results fetching — the host owns the suggestion list and the view filters what it is given — no voice input, and no empty-state prop: empty results always render the empty-search recovery block, so no-results is a named state with its clear recovery rather than silence. The palette is a labelled dialog, choosing reports through select and closes it, and Escape dismisses through the dialog root.

## Native

### Features

Reach for the search view when finding needs a surface: the inline or sheet search over suggestions — the native twin under the same contract. `suggestions` are data — id, title, optional description and leading node — filtered live as the query changes, with `presentation` picking inline or sheet and the open and query trios making it controlled or uncontrolled either way. `onSearch` is the explicit submit, separate from typing, and there is no global hotkey: window-level keybindings are a desktop affordance and the surface opens from the host's own control. There is no results fetching — the host owns the suggestion list and the view filters what it is given — no voice input, and no empty-state prop: empty results always render the empty-search recovery block, so no-results is a named state with its clear recovery rather than silence. Inline renders the results in place while sheet renders them in a bottom sheet — the palette is a placement rather than a dialog.
